_notes.citation_mismatch: The prompt cites 'Chen, Hribar, & Melessa (2017), Financial Restatements and Cash Holdings.' The uploaded PDF is actually Chen, Chen, Dhaliwal, & Huang (2017/2020) in JAAF. Extraction is from the uploaded paper.
_notes.did_structure: No explicit Treat x Post interaction term appears in the regression. The paper uses a SPLIT-SAMPLE DiD design: equation (1) is estimated separately on the restatement subsample (columns 1, 3, 5) and the matched control subsample (columns 2, 4, 6). The treatment effect is the post-estimation DIFFERENCE between the POST coefficients across the two regressions, reported in the 'Test of difference in the coefficient of POST' row. This is mathematically equivalent to a fully-saturated Treat x Post interaction with separate slopes for every covariate.
_notes.panel_choice: Panel A (Baseline) is reported above as the 'main' table. Panel B (Expanded Model) adds CAPX, ACQUISITION, R&D, DIV, DEBT_XFIN, EQUITY_XFIN, MATURITY, NO_LOAN, N_FINCOV, N_GENCOV, and BigN as additional controls but is framed as a robustness check, not the baseline.
_notes.standard_errors: Standard errors clustered at both the matched-pair and year levels (Gow, Ormazabal, & Taylor 2010).
_notes.sample_splits: The table reports three sample partitions: (i) all restatements [cols 1-2], (ii) error restatements [cols 3-4], (iii) irregularity restatements [cols 5-6]. The headline DiD effect (significant at 1%) is in the irregularity sample.
